<main class="site-main"><section class="page-intro"><p class="section-number">Article · Evidence and belief</p><h1>US Presidential Elections — A Bayesian Perspective</h1><div class="article-meta"><span class="status">in bloom</span><span>12 Jan 2025</span></div></section><article class="prose"><p>I want to be a pollster too. This article treats election polling as a model of uncertain information, rather than as a single number waiting to be read aloud.</p><h2>The question</h2><p>How should a forecast change when new polling evidence arrives, and which assumptions are doing the quiet work?</p><h2>What the model makes visible</h2><p>Prior expectations, poll uncertainty, and state-level aggregation each contribute to the final distribution. A probability is not a promise; it is a summary of the model and the information that entered it.</p><p>The original analysis includes a Nevada-focused visualization and the frozen model outputs listed in the migration manifest.</p></article></main>
